newsitem.title: USA: Coral Energy sells 38 trillion Btu of natgas.
newsitem.headline: Coral Energy sells 38 trillion Btu of natgas.

text.p: Coral Energy Resources LP said Tuesday it closed an agreemnt with the Municipal Gas Authority of Georgia to provide 38 trillion Btu of firm natural gas supplies over the next 10 years, receiving $58.6 million.
This is the second such agreement the authority closed in two months to provide long-term, reliable supplies, said Arthur Corbin, MGAG's president and general manager.
In late October in paid Texaco Inc over $112 million under a similar, 10-year agreement, he said.
Corbin said both payments were funded through the sxale of tax exempt revenue bonds.

Coral, a limited partnership between the Royal Dutch/Shell Group's Shell Oil Co and Tejas Gas Corp, will deliver the natural gas on a firm basis into El Paso Energy Corp's the Tennessee Gas Pipeline Co pipeline system for the authority.
Coral spokesman Jimmie Fox declined to discuss how the partnership is accounting for the payment.
Corbin said "These deliveries represent the remaining portion of (natural) gas supplies for our new service to the Tennessee Natural Gas Acquisition Corp."
He said the Tennessee municipalities -- Clarksville and Springfield -- served by that system will pay for transportation of the natural gas.
Corbin said the payment to Coral was based on "the 10-year forward curve" for the Tennessee Gas Pipeline and "a negotiated discount rate."

The Municipal Gas Authority of Georgia is a joint action agency that provides gas supply and related services to municipalities that own and operate natural gas distribution systems in Georgia, Alabama and Florida.
MGAG has been in operation since 1987 and currently serves 73 member cities.
Corbin said it previously arranged three five-to-six year purchase agreements with units of Apache Corp, British Petroleum Co Plc and Shell in 1991, purchasing $150 million of natural gas reserveds.
